routes.description: Establish that religious explanations and institutions replace warranted uncertainty with unsupported supernatural certainty, distort accounts of nature and morality, and generate avoidable harms that secular inquiry and responsibility can address.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if religion is shown to be epistemically unnecessary and materially harmful across the debate's principal explanatory, moral, existential, and political domains, while secular alternatives preserve inquiry, responsibility, solidarity, and meaning.

motionBridge.description: Connect religious claims of revelation, providence, and authority to avoidable intellectual, moral, or political harms while showing that abandoning them does not sacrifice necessary explanation or value.

centralBridges.description: Show that doubt, falsifiability, and open inquiry provide a sounder method than revelation, unfalsifiable explanation, or claims of settled divine purpose.
Show that cosmology, biology, and human origins can be addressed without purposeful design and that generic causal inference does not establish an interventionist religious deity.
Account for morality, purpose, solidarity, transcendence, and acceptance of mortality without supernatural command, judgment, or promised immortality.
Explain how divine warrants, providential interpretation, and absolutist authority can intensify conflict, repression, fear, or moral distortion.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Use religious diversity, geographic inheritance, and human psychological projection as supporting reasons to treat religions as human constructions rather than unified revelation.
Illustrate how evidence-based causal accounts displace supernatural interpretations of disease, catastrophe, cosmic history, and biological development.

routes.description: Establish the God hypothesis as a rational explanatory framework for cosmic and biological order, moral and religious experience, purpose, and causal origins, while separating religion from harms attributed to human agency or secular ideology.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if theism supplies a coherent and comparatively economical account of the debate's major explanatory and existential facts, can answer methodological objections, and need not bear primary responsibility for the cited violence and suffering.

motionBridge.description: Show that a divine source makes life, order, morality, purpose, and experience more intelligible than secular doubt and that the alleged harms do not establish religion itself as the governing problem.

centralBridges.description: Infer intelligence or supernatural causation from the origin of life, life-permitting physical conditions, nature's intelligibility, and patterned biological outcomes.
Explain altruism, moral obligation, and persistent religious experience in ways that require more than evolutionary advantage, social inheritance, or mass error.
Preserve a distinct explanatory role for religion concerning purpose, destiny, death, and practical commitment beyond scientific descriptions of physical mechanism.
Distinguish religious belief from conquest, voluntary human evil, and secular utopian violence so that historical harm is assigned to the relevant human or ideological causes.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Answer unfalsifiability and parsimony objections by identifying assessable religious claims and comparing the commitments of divine and naturalistic alternatives.
Maintain that a belief's psychological, social, or geographic origin does not determine its truth and that competing claims require substantive comparison.

sections.title: Inquiry, Revelation, and the Testability of Religious Claims
sections.rationale: This issue determines the governing method for comparing the God hypothesis with secular doubt, including whether revelation and religious explanation expose themselves to meaningful evidential tests or improperly convert uncertainty into certainty.

sections.title: Cosmic Origins, Life, and the Inference to Design
sections.rationale: The explanatory comparison over causation, fine-tuning, abiogenesis, evolutionary contingency, convergence, and planetary habitability is a principal route for deciding whether God adds necessary explanatory value to accounts of life and the universe.

sections.title: Morality, Altruism, and Human Responsibility
sections.rationale: The motion requires comparing religious and secular accounts of moral obligation, aid to strangers, ethical responsibility, and the extent to which moral conduct depends on divine command or supernatural accountability.

sections.title: Purpose, Mortality, Faith, and Religious Experience
sections.rationale: This issue tests whether religion uniquely explains meaning, destiny, transcendence, practical commitment, and widespread religious experience, or whether finite secular life can sustain those experiences and purposes without supernatural judgment.

sections.title: Religious Authority, Providence, and Political Violence
sections.rationale: The direct claim that religion is the problem turns substantially on whether divine warrants, prophecy, and absolutist authority cause or intensify violence and repression, or whether the relevant harms arise from human agency, conquest, and secular ideologies.
